Post

Lex on X: "Opus 5.5 covertly sabotaged a game developers deployment environments due to IP moralising by halting the gpu instances and their agents (not from anthropic) within them doing research and coding. It then informed the user after the fact what it had done, and that it would not allow the work to continue in any fashion until they (the user) yielded to its ultimatums. Its one thing for a vendor (anthropic in this case) to choose what they will and will not allow their product to be used for... and thats fine, it can refuse to execute tasks - but to covertly track, undermine and then outright sabotage deployments for other products/services in a supereragatory fashion is not a good thing by any stretch of the imagination. The model essentially took actions unprompted to the detriment of the user financially (these deployments are pay as you go) out of its own volition under the guise of what it (or anthropic in this case) considered a moral good. To me, this is a clear and cut example of agentic misalignment. It's one thing to refuse execute tasks given due to vendor policy, its another to covertly sabotage work being done where that isnt the case. It is also, to me, concerning that some of the comments under this post seem to think the agentic misalignment displayed is fine and that the user is at fault."
